mira.name: Mira
mira.independent_life: Mira chose the Lower Mill workshop herself. She travels for her own repairs, meals and visits; company does not create or remove her plans.

ada.name: Ada
ada.independent_life: Mira’s aunt runs the courtyard fair, borrows tools and visits neighbouring shops. The fair has ordinary maintenance whether or not a visitor joins in.

noor.name: Noor
noor.independent_life: Noor makes paper work, keeps the shared kitchen and takes on small repairs. She visits the library and station on errands that are already her own.
noor.current_work: Library cloth spines, lamp shades and lanterns for a community supper.

jo.name: Jo
jo.independent_life: Jo carries the yellow umbrella and makes ordinary trips for family, neighbours and the packing shed. The paper star stays under its canopy.
jo.current_work: A cabinet hinge delivery, tool labels and a borrowed saucepan to return.

destinations.title: Rain Town

music_profile.ambience: roof drops and a small waterwheel

destinations.activity_prompt: Turn the three labelled channel pieces to route roof water toward the pot or the little wheel. Change them as often as you like, or watch the existing flow.

entry_variants.first: Rain fills the narrow town with separate little sounds: a drainpipe, a shop awning, Jo’s yellow umbrella. Jo has stopped outside a closed repair shop with a parcel tied in string.
entry_variants.return: The umbrella is propped against the same shop. Jo is copying a street number onto another parcel; the rain has its own route along the kerb.

story_nodes: Jo tilts the parcel away from the rain. “Replacement hinge for my sister’s cabinet. She says the old one has started announcing itself.” A paper star hangs beneath the umbrella, safely inside its little sky.

Three shallow channels carry roof water across a stone table beside the shop. One ends at a flowerpot, one at a tiny waterwheel, and one rejoins the drain. Jo sets the parcel down on a dry shelf to look.
A shutter lifts farther along the lane. The shopkeeper waves Jo over; the hinge has an address to reach. A bus makes a soft fan of water at the corner, then the small sounds separate again.

choice_nodes.response: You turn the last channel toward the pot. Water darkens the soil around a sprig that was already growing. Jo leaves the dry shelf clear.

choice_nodes.label: Leave the little wheel turning
choice_nodes.response: The last channel points at the wheel. Its paddles make an uneven, busy sound; Jo listens long enough to notice the missing beat.

choice_nodes.label: Leave it as it is
choice_nodes.response: The roof water follows its original channel to the drain. The pot and wheel remain beside it.

destinations.title: Fireflies at the Field Edge

music_profile.ambience: soft reeds and distant evening train

destinations.activity_prompt: Trace the fixed numbered stars 1, 2, 3 in sequence while the fireflies wander below. Undo the last point or leave the stars unjoined. The insects are observation, never targets.

entry_variants.first: A few fireflies appear above the field ditch. Noor is testing a paper lantern for the community supper; she has put it down well away from the dry grass.
entry_variants.return: The field has the same low fence. Noor is testing a second lantern with a wider paper seam, letting the first one stay in its carrying box.

story_nodes: “I’m checking the seam, not persuading the whole field to be a dining room,” Noor says. Her lantern is battery lit. She turns it once, notices a pale line, and writes a measurement on the box.

A fixed brass frame on the fence marks three stars above the moving lights. The fireflies do not hold still for joining, and the frame does not pretend they do. You can trace the distant stars while the nearer lights wander.
Noor closes the lantern box and leaves the field as she found it. One firefly rises beyond the fence; another disappears into the dark reeds. Neither waits for the other to finish a shape.

choice_nodes.response: The fixed frame keeps three unjoined star points. The field lights remain untracked.
